title: Toast the operator for waiting decisions and notable task changes, with a status-line count
description:
Operator instruction, first-party in the opum-doc session 2026-10-03, verbatim: "add toast alerts to the quest mode - when there are open decisions for me, status changes, etc. that I should be notified about". Design by opum-doc under constitution Article 5 clause 1 as amended: opum-doc docs/reference/quest-board-alerts-design.md (opum-ai/opum-doc#630, main 3d47205), relayed by opum-agent as seq 175 on OPAG-1089.

Alerts that toast, and for how long:
- a decision becomes `proposed` -- "DEC-140 needs a decision: (title)", 10 s, never batched;
- a `proposed` decision is resolved -- "DEC-140 decided: accepted", 6 s;
- a task moves to Paused -- "OPAG-777 paused in quest-cli: (title)", 8 s;
- a task moves to Closed -- "LCLI-660 closed (won't do) in lore-cli", 6 s;
- a HIGH-priority task moves to Done -- "OPAG-777 done: (title)", 6 s.
Everything else appears in the pane only and does not toast.

Batching: more than three alert-worthy changes in one check become one toast -- "5 updates: 3 done, 2 paused. Open /quest for the list." Decisions are never folded into a batch.

Status line: while any decision is `proposed`, a `$.ui.status` entry "Quest: 1 decision waiting", cleared when none are. A toast can be missed; the status line stays.

Polling: every 2 minutes whether or not the pane is open, since an alert matters most when the pane is closed. A task that leaves the open set gets ONE `quest task view`, to tell Done from Closed. The full board still refreshes only while the pane is visible.

No replays: the last state seen -- decision ids and statuses, open task ids and statuses -- is kept in `$.store`. The first check after install records a baseline and shows nothing. After a reload or restart the check compares against the stored state. Changes that happened while no session ran arrive as one summary toast, "While you were away: 1 decision waiting, 4 updates", plus the status-line count.

Quiet failure: a repository that cannot be read is skipped for that check and the board's existing "Could not read" line covers it. The check never toasts about its own read errors.

Setting: a `userConfig` option `alerts` -- `all` (default), `decisions` (decision toasts and the count only), `off`.

Heads-up recorded, not acted on: opum-doc is designing an operator-question record with the operator, which may change how "decisions waiting" is counted. Build to the design as it stands.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A new proposed decision toasts once and sets the status-line count, and resolving it toasts and clears the count
Paused, Closed and high-priority Done each toast, and a normal-priority Done does not
More than three alert-worthy changes in one check produce one batched toast, and decisions are never folded into it
Nothing toasts on the first, baseline check; a stored state suppresses repeats after a reload
the alerts userConfig offers all, decisions and off, and off produces no toast
The check runs every 2 minutes with the pane closed, and a task leaving the open set gets exactly one task view to tell Done from Closed
README read failure stays quiet: an unreadable repository produces no toast

plan: 1. Pure helpers in hooks/quest.ts: decision list parser, task-outcome parser, the stored-state shape, the change diff, and the toast/away/status text; 2. The check and its clock in hooks/register.tsx: reads, one task view per departed task, quiet per-repository failure, batching, the baseline and the away summary, and the status line; 3. The alerts userConfig option in .claude-plugin/plugin.json; 4. The nine behavioural tests in tests/board.test.tsx, driven by the mocked clock; 5. Control runs: the pre-change tree, and one mutant per behaviour, each with a predicted red set; 6. Gates: test:mod, typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check, test.
implementationNotes: Shipped on branch feat/QCLI-442-board-alerts (rebased onto origin/dev ca618726). Pure half in hooks/quest.ts: parseAlerts, decisionListArgs, parseDecisionList, parseTaskOutcome, isAlertsState, alertChanges, alertToasts, batchLine, awayLine, waitingStatus. Wiring in hooks/register.tsx: readAlerts, lookUpTask, setWaiting, checkAlerts, startAlerts -- started from session.start and from the first Pane draw. .claude-plugin/plugin.json gains the alerts userConfig option (all default, decisions, off). tests/board.test.tsx gains nine tests driven by the mocked clock.

Decisions taken where the design is silent, each visible in the code and its tests: (1) the stored state keys a decision by repo:id, not by id -- a decision id is minted per workspace, so the same DEC-N in two trackers is two decisions; the toast still prints only the id, as designed. (2) The status-line count is a standing count, not a change notification, so the baseline check pins it too; the design says the first check shows nothing, read as no toasts. (3) alerts off returns before any read, writes no state, and clears a count this session pinned. (4) The batch toast stays 8 s; the design gives timeouts for the table rows only. (5) The away summary counts decisions that became proposed plus alert-worthy task changes; a decision resolved while no session ran is not reported in it. (6) A resolution kind is humanised for the toast (wont-do reads as the two words with an apostrophe); other kinds print as they are, and a Closed record with no resolution prints without the parenthetical.

Control runs, every one with the new tests kept and the run recorded in full: (a) pre-change tree (hooks and plugin.json reverted to 164aa550) -- 6 of the 9 new tests red: waiting decision, paused/closed/done, batch, baseline, away summary, poll-with-pane-closed. (b) the option ignored (parseAlerts always all) -- exactly 1 red, the off test. (c) the stored state ignored -- 7 red, including the stored-state test no other mutant reddens. (d) the readable-repository guard removed -- exactly 1 red, the unreadable-repository test. (e) the batch threshold and the high-priority Done guard removed -- exactly 2 red, the batch test and the paused/closed/done test. (f) the state never written back -- 4 red, the replay assertion and the poll test among them. (g) the baseline branch made to toast -- 6 red. No pre-existing test went red in any run.

Gates on the rebased head, each run from the worktree: test:mod exit 0 (31 pass, 0 fail; its typecheck step reports NOT TYPECHECKED -- this machine carries declarations for Claude Code 2.1.286/2.1.287 and the running CLI is 2.1.288, so the mod was not typechecked by that step; the same check was run by hand against the 2.1.287 declaration and was clean). typecheck 0, lint 0, format:check 0, layer:check 0. test exits 1 with exactly one failure, test/qcli411-bun-declare-binding.test.ts, which is this machine running bun 1.3.14 against the pinned 1.4.2: 1081 pass, 1 fail.

Two things routed, not decided here. (1) The batch toast ends with the design's own words, Open /quest for the list. On this head the board still registers the quest-board slash command, but QCLI-440's decided outcome recorded on dev (ca618726) is that the board registers no slash command at all, and that a session.start hook that registers one is refused outright. Once QCLI-440 lands, that sentence names a command that does not exist. Built to the design because the design binds; the wording needs a design call. (2) docs/reference/quest-board-hooks-module-in-the-opum-quest-plugin.md now under-describes the module: its manifest row lists the actor, root and repos options and not alerts. Left alone -- the dispatch scoped the change to the hooks, the manifest and the mod tests, and docs here are driven through lore.
